drafted_from: workflow:build-a-best-x-for-y-comparison's row in tools/workflows/recipes/workflows.json (its input schema, steps and submit shapes)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:build-a-best-x-for-y-comparison for bakery point-of-sale software for a one-shop bakery with 3 staff, publishing at https://example.com/best, checked against my writing rules."
no_lists_because: The page, its proofs and scores are written to the person's own site and the step answers, not to a list.
instructions: 1. Choose X (the category in buyers' words) and Y (the buyer), the address where you publish, one answer engine search address with {question} in it, and the id of your writing rules.
2. Say "Run workflow:build-a-best-x-for-y-comparison" with those values; add vendors you know and any sponsors with their disclosure words.

3. The AI works scope, metrics, gather-proof, score, page, publish and keep-cited: vendors named by answer engines, only metrics a vendor can prove at a public address, each value read with its address and date, scores from tool:classify-a-record, then the page.
4. Approve the page exactly as shown before it is published; sponsored placement stays in its own labelled block and never changes a score.
5. Read the keep-cited answer for the workflow it handed the page to and the date every proof is read again.

worked_examples.title: Three vendors are scored from three provable metrics
worked_examples.ask: Rank bakery point-of-sale software for a one-shop bakery.
worked_examples.given: The metrics step kept three signals with weights: uptime-public 3 (a public status page), price-public 2 (a public price page) and customer-stories 2 (named stories). The gather-proof step found Ovenly POS proves all three, CrumbDesk proves uptime-public and price-public, LoafLedger proves only price-public. A vendor's score is the weights of the signals that fired, and ties go by name; read from the score step of the workflow row.
